{{Nihongo|'''The Substitute Shinigami arc'''|死神代行篇|Shinigami Daikō-hen}} is the first season of the ''[[Bleach (TV series)|Bleach]]'' [[anime]] television series. The episodes are directed by [[Noriyuki Abe]], and produced by [[TV Tokyo]], [[Dentsu]], and [[Studio Pierrot]].<ref name="staff">{{#invoke:Cite|web|url=http://pierrot.jp/title/bleach/staff.html|script-title=ja:ぴえろブリーチ|publisher=[[Studio Pierrot]]|language=ja|access-date=April 7, 2009}}</ref> In the English release by [[Viz Media]], the title is changed to simply '''The Substitute'''.<ref name="Viz DVD">{{#invoke:Cite|web|url=http://www.viz.com/products/products.php?product_id=6112 |title=VIZ Media . products - Bleach - Vol. 1 (DVD) |access-date=May 23, 2007|url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090210165824/http://viz.com/products/products.php?product_id=6112 |archive-date=February 10, 2009}} Viz media product info for ''Bleach'' DVD collection 01 on the Viz website.</ref> The season adapts the first eight volumes (chapters 1–70) of [[Tite Kubo]]'s ''[[Bleach (manga)|Bleach]]'' [[manga]] series, spanning twenty episodes. The episodes' plot covers the adventures of a high school student [[Ichigo Kurosaki]] after becoming a [[Soul Reaper (Bleach)|Soul Reaper]] and assuming the duties of Soul Reaper [[Rukia Kuchiki]].

The first season aired from October 2004 to February 2005 on [[TV Tokyo]]. The first English airing of the series was from September 2006 to January 2007. It was shown on [[YTV (Canadian TV channel)|YTV]]'s [[Bionix (TV programming block)|Bionix]] programming block in Canada and [[Cartoon Network]]'s [[Adult Swim]] in the United States,<ref>{{#invoke:Cite|web|url=http://www.animenewsnetwork.com/news/2006-03-30/adult-swim-picks-up-bleach|first=Jonathan|last=May|title=Adult Swim Picks up Bleach|date=March 30, 2006|website=[[Anime News Network]]|publisher=Kadokawa Group|access-date=April 12, 2009}}</ref> with Bionix airing the show one day sooner. The arc started airing in the United Kingdom starting in September 2007 on [[AnimeCentral]].<ref>{{#invoke:Cite|web|url=http://www.animenewsnetwork.com/news/2007-09-13/uk's-animecentral-channel-launches-on-sky-digital|first=Egan|last=Loo|title=UK's AnimeCentral Channel Launches on Sky Digital|date=September 13, 2007|website=[[Anime News Network]]|publisher=Kadokawa Group|access-date=April 12, 2009}}</ref>

The episodes use three pieces of theme music: one opening theme and two ending themes. The opening theme is [[Orange Range]]'s single "[[Asterisk (song)|Asterisk]]".<ref name="music1">{{#invoke:Cite|web|url=http://www.tv-tokyo.co.jp/anime/bleach/staff.html|script-title=ja:ブリーチ|publisher=[[TV Tokyo]]|access-date=April 8, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040925002611/http://www.tv-tokyo.co.jp/anime/bleach/staff.html|archive-date=September 25, 2004|language=ja }}</ref> The ending theme for the first thirteen episodes is "Life is Like a Boat" by [[Rie Fu]],<ref name="music1" /> while the remaining seven used "Thank You!!" by [[Home Made Kazoku]].<ref>{{#invoke:Cite|web|url=http://www.tv-tokyo.co.jp/anime/bleach/staff.html|script-title=ja:ブリーチ|publisher=[[TV Tokyo]]|access-date=April 8, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050207042739/http://www.tv-tokyo.co.jp/anime/bleach/staff.html|archive-date=February 7, 2005|language=ja}}</ref>

The arc was released on five DVD compilations, each containing four episodes of the show. They were released in Japan from February 2 to June 1, 2005.<ref>{{#invoke:Cite|web|url=http://www.aniplex.co.jp/bleach/dvd/dvd01.html|script-title=ja:死神代行篇|publisher=[[Aniplex]]|access-date=December 31, 2009|language=ja }}</ref> Viz Media's release of the DVDs was made from November 5 to July 31, 2007.<ref name="Viz DVD"/><ref name="VizDVD5">{{#invoke:Cite|web|url=http://www.viz.com/products/products.php?product_id=6704 |title=Bleach, Vol. 5 (DVD) |publisher=[[Viz Media]] |access-date=January 17, 2009|url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090210165835/http://viz.com/products/products.php?product_id=6704 |archive-date=February 10, 2009}}</ref> The first of these compilations, with art featuring the series main character Ichigo Kurosaki, was nominated at the [[American Anime Awards]] in 2007 for best DVD package design.<ref name="Awards">{{#invoke:Cite|web|url=http://comics.ign.com/articles/764/764384p1.html|title=NYCC 07: Viz Anime Dominates Award Noms|website=[[IGN]]|publisher=IGN Entertainment, inc.|first=Richard|last=George|date=February 13, 2007|access-date=March 26, 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070818192721/http://comics.ign.com/articles/764/764384p1.html|archive-date=2007-08-18|url-status=dead}}</ref> A DVD collection box, containing all twenty episodes of the arc, was released by Viz Media on October 30, 2007.<ref name="VizDVDCollection">{{#invoke:Cite|web|url=http://www.viz.com/products/products.php?product_id=7184 |title=VIZ Media . products - Bleach Uncut Season 1 (DVD Box Set) |publisher=[[Viz Media]] |access-date=December 25, 2007|url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071209221649/http://www.viz.com/products/products.php?product_id=7184 |archive-date=December 9, 2007}}</ref> [[Manga Entertainment]] released two DVDs containing the first season in the United Kingdom on November 5, 2007, and March 3, 2008.<ref>{{#invoke:Cite|web|url=https://www.amazon.co.uk/dp/B000W2FIAI/|title=Bleach - Series 1 Part 1|website=Amazon UK |access-date=April 14, 2011}}</ref><ref>{{#invoke:Cite|web|url=https://www.amazon.co.uk/dp/B0010LAZVW/|title=Bleach - Series 1 Part 2|website=Amazon UK |access-date=April 14, 2014}}</ref> A compilation of these two volumes was released on May 5, 2008.<ref>{{#invoke:cite|web|url=https://www.amazon.co.uk/dp/B0013URJV4/|title=Bleach Complete Series 1|website=Amazon UK |access-date=April 14, 2007}}</ref>

{{Episode list/sublist|Bleach season 1
| EpisodeNumber   = 1
| EpisodeNumber2  = 1
| Title           = The Day I Became a Shinigami
| TranslitTitle   = Shinigami ni Natchatta Hi
| NativeTitle     = 死神になっちゃった日
| NativeTitleLangCode = ja
| DirectedBy      = [[Noriyuki Abe]]
| WrittenBy       = Masashi Sogo

| OriginalAirDate = {{Start date|2004|10|5}}
| AltDate         = September 10, 2006
| ShortSummary    = [[Ichigo Kurosaki]] is a fifteen-year-old high school student with orange hair, brown eyes, and the ability to see spirits. As he tries to protect the spirit of a little girl from a [[List of Hollows in Bleach#hollow|hollow]], he witnesses a clash between the [[malevolent spirit]] and a female [[List of Soul Reapers in Bleach|Soul Reaper]]. Later, Ichigo is met by the same woman again in his room. She introduces herself as [[Rukia Kuchiki]], and explains to Ichigo the basic duty of the Soul Reapers is the act of soul cleansing. The hollow, named [[List of Hollows in Bleach#Fishbone D|Fishbone D]], returns to absorb Ichigo's high spiritual energy, attacking Ichigo's home, and Rukia is wounded. In order to save his family, Ichigo desperately takes Rukia’s power into himself and becomes a Soul Reaper to successfully defeat the hollow.
| LineColor       = 485858
}}

| AltDate         = September 24, 2006
| ShortSummary    = Ichigo discovers that one of his schoolmates, [[Orihime Inoue]], is being stalked by her older brother's spirit who turned into the hollow [[List of Hollows in Bleach#Acidwire|Acidwire]] due to Orihime stopping her prayers for him, which makes him hesitate to fulfill his duty. As Ichigo is forced to use his power again, his qualms of killing hollows are rested and he finally submits to his purpose as a substitute Soul Reaper, killing Acidwire. Before he does so however, Orihime's older brother was able to revert to his kind and gentle nature, expressing his love for her and thanking her before being sent to the Soul Society, the place where Soul Reapers and souls reside, via Ichigo's zanpakuto.
| LineColor       = 485858
}}

| ShortSummary    = As his last day of school ends, Ichigo is upset to discover that no one except for Orihime, Chad and Uryū seems to remember Rukia, due to a mind wipe imposed by the Soul Society. He begins his training at the Urahara Shop, first battling the shop's girl assistant, [[List of Bleach characters#Ururu Tsumugiya|Ururu Tsumugiya]] to regain control of his spirit body. As the training enters stage two, Ichigo's soul is cut from his body and thrown into a pit. He must regain his Soul Reaper powers within three days, or risk becoming a hollow. Meanwhile, [[List of Bleach characters#Yoruichi Shihōin|Yoruichi Shihōin]], a talking cat, offers to train Chad and Orihime to control and enhance their powers so they can join Ichigo to go to the Soul Society and rescue Rukia.

| ShortSummary    = While fighting Urahara, Ichigo learns that Zangetsu is the name of his ''zanpakutō''. Upon learning the name, the sword transforms into its more powerful ''shikai'' form as Ichigo unleashes an energy blast which knocks off Urahara's hat, completing the third stage in his training. Orihime and Chad, meanwhile, finish their training with Yoruichi. The entire group, including Uryū, who has been training alone, set out for the Soul Society using a gate that Yoruichi and Urahara made.
